items.text: Examples of group functors
\mathbb G_a\colon k'\mapsto(k',+),\qquad \mathbb G_m\colon k'\mapsto k'^{*}
\mathcal O\colon k'\mapsto k'\ \ (\text{ring functor}),\qquad \mathbb G_a=\mathcal O\ \text{(addition only)},\qquad \mathbb G_m\subset\mathcal O^{\bullet}\ \text{(multiplication)}
$\mathbb G_m$ = largest group object contained in the monoid object $\mathcal O^{\bullet}$.

\begin{array}{lll} \mathbb G_a & \leftrightarrow & k[t]\\ \mathbb G_m & \leftrightarrow & k[t,t^{-1}]\\ \mathrm{GL}_n & \leftrightarrow & k[t_{ij}]_{1\le i,j\le n}[1/\Delta],\ \ \Delta=\det(t_{ij})\end{array}
$O(Q)(k')=\{g\in\mathrm{GL}_n(k') : Q\circ g=Q\}$ — stabiliser of a point (the form $Q$); representable by the stabiliser argument.
Triangular subgroups
T_n(k')=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_1&&*\\&\ddots&\\0&&\lambda_n\end{pmatrix}:\ \lambda_i\in k'^{*}\right\}
T_n\simeq\{(x_{ij})_{i\le j}:\ x_{ij}\in k',\ x_{ii}\in k'^{*}\}\simeq \mathbb A^{n(n-1)/2}\times\mathbb G_m^{\,n}
T_n\ \text{represented by}\ k[t_{ij}\,(i\le j)]\,[t_{11}^{-1},\dots,t_{nn}^{-1}]
Strictly triangular subgroup (ones on the diagonal): represented by $k[t_{ij}]_{i<j}$.
The hyperbola
G(k')=\{(x,y)\in k'^2 : xy=1\},\ \text{coordinatewise product};\qquad \mathcal O(G)=k[x,y]/(xy-1)=k[x,x^{-1}]\ \simeq\mathbb G_m
Embeddings of $\mathbb G_m$ and $\mathbb G_a$ in $\mathrm{GL}_n$
\mathbb G_m\to\mathrm{GL}_n,\qquad \lambda\mapsto\lambda\cdot 1_n=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda,\dots,\lambda)\quad(\text{monomorphism, central})
\mathbb G_m\to\mathrm{GL}_n,\qquad \lambda\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(1,\dots,\lambda,\dots,1)\ (\lambda\ \text{in the } i\text{-th place})\quad(\text{not central})
Centre of a group object

$u\colon Z\to G$, $Z$ an object of $C$, $G$ a group object. $u\in G(Z)$ being central in the group $G(Z)$ is not stable under base change $Z'\to Z$ (a homomorphism need not send centre to centre); so define a subfunctor.
A morphism $Z\to G$ = a section of $G_Z=G\times Z$ over $Z$; a section $g'$ of a group $G'$ defines the inner automorphism (functorial in $k''$):
x\mapsto g'xg'^{-1}\ \ \text{on}\ G'(k''),\ \text{for every}\ k''\ \text{over}\ k'
G\longrightarrow \underline{\operatorname{Aut}}(G),\qquad Z\mapsto\operatorname{Aut}(G_Z)\quad(\text{operation of } G \text{ on itself by inner automorphisms})
Centre of a group object $G$: the subgroup functor
\mathcal C=\operatorname{Ker}\bigl(G\to\underline{\operatorname{Aut}}(G)\bigr)
$u\in G(Z)$ is in the centre iff its image in $G(Z')$ is central for every $Z'\to Z$ (not only in $G(Z)$).
If $G$ is an affine algebraic group over a field, the centre is again one (not proved here); over a ring it needs hypotheses.
$\mathbb G_m\to\mathrm{GL}_n$, $\lambda\mapsto\lambda 1_n$ is central: a scalar matrix commutes with all matrices, over any $k''$.
$\underline{\operatorname{Aut}}(\mathbb G_a)$ over a field of characteristic $p>0$ or over $\mathbb Z$ is not representable (neither affine nor a group scheme); it is an ind-scheme.
\mathbb G_a\to\mathrm{GL}_2\to\mathrm{GL}_n,\qquad \lambda\mapsto\begin{pmatrix}1&\lambda\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\mapsto\begin{pmatrix}1&\lambda&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1_{n-2}\end{pmatrix}
Automorphisms of $k'^2$ inducing the identity on the sub $k'$ and on the quotient $k'$.
Over a field every affine algebraic group of finite type is a subgroup of some $\mathrm{GL}_n$ (to be proved later).
The functor $W(M)$
W(M)\colon k'\mapsto M\otimes_k k'\qquad(\text{a module over the ring functor }\mathcal O)
M\simeq k^n\ \Longrightarrow\ W(M)\simeq(k'\mapsto k'^n)=\mathbb A^n
Claim. $M$ projective of finite type (direct factor of a free module of finite type) $\Rightarrow W(M)$ representable.
Proof. $M=\operatorname{Ker}(1-p)$, $p$ a projector of $L=k^m$; then $M\otimes k'=\operatorname{Ker}\bigl((1-p)\otimes k'\bigr)$ in $L\otimes k'$, so
W(M)=\operatorname{Ker}\bigl(W(L)\xrightarrow{\,1-p\,}W(L)\bigr)=W(L)\times_{W(L)}\{0\}
Converse. $W(M)$ representable $\Rightarrow$ $M$ projective of finite type. Two properties of a representable $F$ (on $k$-algebras):
(a) $k'\hookrightarrow k''$ injective $\Rightarrow F(k')\to F(k'')$ injective ($F(k')=\operatorname{Hom}(A,k')$).
(b) $F$ commutes with arbitrary products:
F\Bigl(\prod_i k_i\Bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\prod_i F(k_i)

(a) gives $M\otimes k'\to M\otimes k''$ injective: $M$ is flat (for $N'\hookrightarrow N$, $M\otimes N'\to M\otimes N$ injective). Converse by taking the algebras $k\oplus N'\to k\oplus N$ with $N',N$ ideals of square zero.
(b) with all $k_i=k$:
M\otimes k^I\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }M^I

An element of $M\otimes k^I$ is a finite sum $\sum_\alpha x_\alpha\otimes y_\alpha$, $x_\alpha\in M$: so $M\otimes k^I$ is the union of the images of $M_\alpha\otimes k^I$, $M_\alpha$ running over the submodules of finite type; thus
M^I=\bigcup_\alpha \operatorname{Im}\bigl(M_\alpha^I\bigr)\qquad (I\ \text{infinite})
